{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-sc-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"e2f4d9f04976b965c490d6be874531ba38c739b485a679f98487bfdcfbff1136","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-sc-class-d:lineage:5","source_registry_sha256":"61c32f86a25e3c021742b3c9ddf64a97709817dd75a19df6d2b69eac0a40c4f1","source_liveness_sha256":"feb7871590284d2a19ab0509ff65b48154ba15e637a6ec9b839f55a72736ffdb"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Skills retests, moving and visiting, renewal, the point system and restricted licenses","heading":"C — Skills test retest waits, out-of-state and international drivers, renewal, the point system, suspensions and restricted licenses","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Skills test retest waits, out-of-state and international drivers, renewal, the point system, suspensions and restricted licenses
Knowledge domain: what happens after a failed skills test, what new residents, temporary residents and visitors must do, how a license is renewed, how points build up and lead to suspension, and which restricted or temporary licenses exist after a suspension.

FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A01
The skills test may also include a forward two-point turnabout, a three-point turnabout and interstate driving. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A01
After failing the skills test on the first try you must wait two business days to retest, whatever your age or experience. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A01
After a second failed skills test the wait is seven calendar days, and after a third or later failure it is 30 calendar days. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A01
A new permanent resident with a valid license or ID from another state must apply for an SC license or ID within 45 days of moving, unless on active military duty or employed by the US Government. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A01
You must surrender your out-of-state license or ID to get an SC one, and an out-of-state license expired over nine months means taking the vision, knowledge and skills tests. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A01
Temporary residents such as military members or students, and their dependents, do not need an SC license but must hold a valid out-of-state license to drive in SC. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A02
When you move away and get a new license or ID in another state, you hand in the SC one there, the new state tells the SCDMV and your SC credential is cancelled. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A02
When registering a vehicle in another state, return your SC plate to the SCDMV before canceling your SC insurance, or you could owe up to $400 in fees. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A02
A permanent resident of another state may drive in SC on a valid license from the home state. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A02
Visitors from non-English-speaking countries are strongly advised to carry an International Driving Permit, which translates the foreign license into English but is not a license itself. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A02
SC waives the knowledge and skills tests for a first-time SC applicant whose out-of-country credential comes from a country with a formal reciprocity agreement with SC. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A03
That reciprocity waiver applies only if the foreign credential has not been expired more than nine months. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A03
Renewing a license requires passing a vision test, and every SCDMV branch offers free vision screenings. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A03
Instead of a branch screening, the SCDMV may take a Certificate of Vision Examination from a licensed eye care professional dated within the past 36 months, which SC-licensed professionals file through the online portal. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A03
Since May 18, 2024, active-duty military personnel skip vision screening when they show a Leave and Earning Statement dated within 31 days of the transaction plus a non-expired military ID. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A03
Only US citizens may renew online, and an online renewal gives an eight-year license. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-F17 | anchor: A03
Online renewal requires a regular license (Class D, E, F, G, M or a combination), no CDL, and a license expired no more than 9 months. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-F18 | anchor: A04
Online renewal also requires a Social Security number and name that match Social Security Administration records and no more than five points in the last two years. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-F19 | anchor: A04
You cannot renew online if your license is suspended or about to be, if you renewed by mail or online last time, if you are listed as a Convicted Violent Offender, or if you hold a conditional or special restricted license. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-F20 | anchor: A04
For online renewal an SC-licensed eye care professional must send the vision certificate electronically, and you pay with a valid credit card at the end. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-F21 | anchor: A04
An online renewal reuses your current photo and signature, and the new license arrives by mail in seven to ten business days. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-F22 | anchor: A05
A mail renewal includes form 447-NC, the vision certificate receipt number or an out-of-state professional's certificate, and a $25 check or money order made out to the SCDMV, never cash. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-F23 | anchor: A05
Mail the renewal at least three weeks before the expiration date, and the SCDMV keeps the photo and signature from your current license. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-F24 | anchor: A05
In-person renewal needs a vision test at the branch or an accepted vision certificate, the name of your vehicle insurance company and a $25 license fee. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-F25 | anchor: A05
Eye care professionals licensed outside SC complete the Certificate of Vision Examination on SCDMV Form 412-NC. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-F26 | anchor: A06
Never drive on an expired license; one expired nine months or less can be renewed at a branch with no testing. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-F27 | anchor: A06
A license expired more than nine months requires a branch visit with vision, knowledge and skills tests, current proof of address and any identity documents not already on file. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-F28 | anchor: A06
Points go on your SC record for traffic convictions in SC or in any other state, and also for a military court-martial traffic conviction. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-F29 | anchor: A06
Points drop by half one year after the violation date on the ticket, so four points from a June ticket become two points the next June. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-F30 | anchor: A07
Drivers aged 15 or 16 get a warning letter from the SCDMV at two points and again at four points, and further violations can cost them their privileges. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-F31 | anchor: A07
Drivers 17 or older get a warning letter at six or more points, and the license is suspended when the total reaches 12 or more. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-F32 | anchor: A07
A beginner's permit, conditional or special restricted holder who reaches six or more points is suspended for excessive points, and a defensive driving course will not reinstate that suspension. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-F33 | anchor: A07
Some violations, such as driving under the influence, carry mandatory suspensions that sit outside the point system. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-F34 | anchor: A07
Points may be reduced by finishing the National Safety Council Defensive Driving Course or an equivalent, which cannot be done online and must be taken in SC. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-F35 | anchor: A08
The point-reduction course must be eight classroom hours, taken after the violation date, and the reduction can be used only once in a three-year period. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec02-F36 | anchor: A08
If your license is in danger of suspension, the course must be finished before the suspension starts, because a reduction will not cancel a suspension already under way. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec02-F37 | anchor: A08
Drivers who owe reinstatement fees on an SC license may pay online and may qualify for a payment plan if they owe at least a minimum amount and follow the plan rules. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec02-F38 | anchor: A09
A first-offense DUI or DUAC suspension may allow a six-month provisional license for $100 with ADSAP enrollment, if the other conditions are met. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec02-F39 | anchor: A09
For a DUI or DUAC on or after October 1, 2014, the provisional license needs a BAC of 0.14 percent or less. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec02-F40 | anchor: A09
The provisional license is not available for any DUI or DUAC that happens on or after May 19, 2024. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec02-F41 | anchor: A09
A non-citizen can get a route-restricted license only with permanent resident alien status. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec02-F42 | anchor: A10
A route-restricted license allows non-commercial driving only to and from work, college or home, ADSAP, or a court-ordered drug program, with the approved route carried in the vehicle. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec02-F43 | anchor: A10
The route-restricted license lasts as long as the suspension, costs $100 if approved, and for most listed suspensions is granted only once in a lifetime. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec02-F44 | anchor: A10
Suspensions for unpaid child support or a first or second driving-under-suspension offense within five years may allow more than one route-restricted license. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec02-F45 | anchor: A11
A Temporary Alcohol License costs $100 and needs an administrative hearing request filed within 30 days for an implied consent, under-21 implied consent, 0.15 BAC or under-21 0.02 BAC suspension. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec02-F46 | anchor: A11
The Temporary Alcohol License works until the SCDMV receives the hearing results, and it must be returned whether the suspension is upheld or overturned. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0028]

Misconceptions: the skills retest wait grows with each failure instead of staying fixed; an International Driving Permit only translates a foreign license and never replaces it; points halve after a year but do not vanish; a defensive driving course cannot lift a suspension that has already started; driving under the influence is handled by mandatory suspension, not points.
Mnemonics: retest waits climb two, seven, thirty, meaning two business days, then seven calendar days, then thirty calendar days; teen letters at two and four points, adult letter at six, suspension at twelve; points halve at one year.
Glossary: DUAC means driving with an unlawful alcohol concentration; ADSAP means the Alcohol and Drug Safety Action Program; route-restricted license means a license limited to an approved route during a suspension; Temporary Alcohol License means a short-term license while an alcohol suspension hearing is pending; Certificate of Vision Examination means an eye care professional's vision report accepted in place of a branch screening.
Dynamic facts: fees, mailing addresses, mailing times, renewal eligibility and the payment plan minimum can change; confirm them on the SCDMV website.
